verdict.rationale: BILL ships its own event-triggered rules in specific domains. Bill approval policies are rule sets that decide which bills need approval, by whom and when. Vendor autopay pays a vendor automatically when a bill is created, and PO tolerance rules govern matching. There is no evidence of a general-purpose, user-definable event-to-action rule engine; webhooks only notify external systems and do not count as in-product rule actions. Missing for 10: a general configurable rules/automation builder covering arbitrary S&E events and actions, documentation of rule conditions and action types, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: A bill approval policy is a set of rules that enables you to control which bills require approval, by whom, and when.
When this feature is enabled for a vendor, BILL automatically pays the vendor when a bill is created for the vendor.
